title: Low-Complexity and Consistent Graphon Estimation from Multiple Networks

split.decision: Synthetic: observations only, opaque shuffled ids. Each collection has M=200, n uniform integers 10..100. No reusable training; train directory empty. Validation 3 trials per graphon with public master seed 20261030; held-out evaluation preserves 20 independent trials per graphon, drawn with secrets and recorded privately. Paper ids 1..11,13; frozen generator; per-instance fitting in predict.

baseline.paper_ref: Table 1 JGS, 12 reproducible graphons: paper 15.0383; reproduction 14.9146; lower bound 0

allowed_changes: Graphon estimation models, auxiliary losses, degree/order estimators, block count/smoothing and numerical methods may change, yielding the required step-function representation.
The JGS automatic block rule and estimator are baseline methods; the score does not compare a fixed Bayesian posterior.
When retaining the supplied JGS estimator, changing only smoothing=False or k=None does not count as a method improvement.
fixed_contract: Estimate the graphon of each fixed collection of observed networks, minimizing its original degree-sorted step-function off-diagonal L2 error.
The latent graphon target, observed collection of 200 undirected networks, twelve selected designs and per-collection inference boundary remain fixed.
Symmetric probability step-matrix output, degree-sort convention, equal-width expansion to the 1000-grid, off-diagonal L2 times 1000 and equal graphon aggregation remain fixed.
Supplied data/splits, evaluation metric, trusted evaluator and lawful information access.
method_freedom_review.budget_policy: agent overall deadline; separate overall formal replay budget
forbidden_substitutions: Do not redefine the target as a resized image or alternative graph metric, replace the fixed degree-sorted loss, or classify graphon identity then return a memorized reference function.
No true latent positions, external/simulated collections, cross-collection fitting or hidden labels/seed lookup.
Training or fitting reusable model state or learned preprocessing on validation features or labels, including final train+val refits or validation-based distillation.
